q.t: A roti is cut into 2 equal parts. What is each part called?
q.e: When a whole is cut into 2 equal parts, each part is one half, written 1/2.

q.t: A paper is folded into 4 equal parts. What is each part called?
q.e: One of 4 equal parts is a quarter, written 1/4.

q.t: How many halves make one whole?
q.e: The whole was cut into 2 equal parts, so 2 halves fit back together.

q.t: How many quarters make one whole?
q.e: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts, so 4 of them make the whole.

q.t: Which is bigger: 1/2 or 1/4 of the same roti?
q.e: Cutting into fewer parts makes each part bigger — 2 parts are bigger than 4 parts.

q.t: What is 1/2 of 10 sweets?
q.e: Share 10 sweets into 2 equal groups: each group has 5.

q.t: Meena has 8 diyas. How many diyas are 1/4 of them?
q.e: Split 8 diyas into 4 equal groups: each group has 2.

q.t: A dhokla is shared equally among 5 people. What part does each get?
q.e: One of 5 equal parts is written 1/5 — one fifth.

q.t: A paper is cut into 2 parts of different sizes. Is each part a half?
o: No — halves must be equal parts
Only the bigger part is a half
Only the smaller part is a half
q.e: A half is one of 2 EQUAL parts, so unequal pieces are not halves.

q.t: How do we read 1/3?
q.e: The 3 below means 3 equal parts, and the 1 above means we take one of them.

q.t: Which is smaller: 1/6 or 1/8 of the same dhokla?
q.e: Sharing among 8 people gives each a smaller piece than sharing among 6.

q.t: Two quarters of a paper are the same as:
q.e: 4 quarters make a whole, so 2 quarters make half of it.

q.t: A box has 16 barfis. How many barfis are 1/4 of the box?
q.e: Split 16 into 4 equal groups: 4 in each.

q.t: There are 12 cookies. How many cookies are 1/3 of them?
q.e: Split 12 into 3 equal groups: 4 in each.

q.t: How many pieces of 1/6 make one whole?
q.e: 1/6 means one of 6 equal parts, so 6 such pieces fit together into the whole.

q.t: A rectangle is cut into 4 equal parts and 3 of them are shaded. What part is shaded?
q.e: 3 of the 4 equal parts are shaded — three quarters, written 3/4.

q.t: A garden has 5 equal parts. Roses grow in 2 of them. What part has roses?
q.e: 2 out of 5 equal parts is 2/5 — the bottom number counts the parts, the top counts the ones we take.

q.t: Which is greater: 1/5 or 1/4 of the same cake?
q.e: 4 equal parts are bigger than 5 equal parts of the same cake.

q.t: 12 cookies are shared equally among 6 children. How many does each child get?
q.e: Give one at a time round the 6 children: after 2 rounds all 12 are gone.

q.t: A garden has 5 equal parts and roses fill all 5. What part has roses?
q.e: Taking all 5 of the 5 equal parts gives the whole.

q.t: 1/2 is the same as which fraction?
q.e: Fold each half into 2 again: the half becomes 2 of 4 equal parts.

q.t: A paper is folded into 3 equal parts and 1 is coloured. Then it is folded in half again. 1/3 is the same as:
q.e: Halving every part makes 6 parts, and the coloured third is now 2 of them.

q.t: How many pieces of 1/8 make 1/4?
q.e: Cut each quarter in half and you get eighths, so one quarter is 2 eighths.

q.t: Three pieces of 1/6 together make:
q.e: 6 sixths make a whole, so 3 sixths make half of it.

q.t: There are 20 pots. How many pots are 3/5 of them?
q.e: 1/5 of 20 is 4, so 3/5 is 3 groups of 4 = 12.

q.t: When will Sumedha get MORE dhokla: when it is shared equally among 9 people or among 11 people?
q.e: Fewer people sharing the same dhokla means bigger pieces.

q.t: A dosa has 1/4 potato, 1/4 onion and the rest tomato. What part is tomato?
q.e: Two quarters are used, so 2 of the 4 quarters are left — that is half.

q.t: Mohan’s ribbon is 1/4 as long as Rohan’s. Mohan’s ribbon is 5 cm. How long is Rohan’s (in cm)?
q.e: Mohan’s is one of 4 equal parts of Rohan’s, so Rohan’s is 4 × 5 cm.

q.t: Which is the smallest: 1/2, 1/3, 1/7 or 1/5?
q.e: The more equal parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part — 7 is the most parts.

q.t: Simran has 15 friends at her party. 1/3 of them get a hairband. How many get a hairband?
q.e: Split 15 friends into 3 equal groups: one group has 5.

q.t: A dhokla is shared equally among 5 people. Idha gives her share to Sumedha. What part does Sumedha have now?
q.e: Her own 1/5 plus Idha’s 1/5 makes 2 of the 5 equal parts.

q.t: A dhokla is shared equally among 5. Both Idha and Vinayak give their shares to Sumedha. What part does Sumedha have now?
q.e: Her 1/5 plus two more fifths makes 3 of the 5 parts.

q.t: 24 laddoos: 1/4 go to Ravi and 1/3 go to Meena. How many laddoos are left?
q.e: Ravi gets 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and Meena gets 24 ÷ 3 = 8; 24 − 6 − 8 = 10.

q.t: A garden has 7 equal parts. Marigold is in 1/7, roses are in 3/7 and hibiscus fills the rest. What part is hibiscus?
q.e: 1 + 3 = 4 parts are used, so 7 − 4 = 3 of the 7 parts are left.

q.t: A ribbon is 1 metre (100 cm) long. How long is 1/4 of it (in cm)?
q.e: Cut 100 cm into 4 equal pieces: each is 25 cm.

q.t: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Ali eats 3 slices and Bina eats 2. What part of the pizza is left?
q.e: 5 of the 8 slices are eaten, so 8 − 5 = 3 slices (3/8) are left.

q.t: 16 barfis: Mummy gives 1/4 of them to Ravi and 1/4 to Sita. How many barfis are left?
q.e: Each child gets 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so 8 are given away and 8 are left — two quarters gone leaves half.

q.t: Which is more: 1/2 of 30 or 1/3 of 60?
q.e: 1/2 of 30 is 15, but 1/3 of 60 is 20.

q.t: Ravi’s dhokla is cut into 6 equal pieces and he eats 2. Rani’s same-size dhokla is cut into 3 equal pieces and she eats 1. Who ate more?
q.e: Halving each of Rani’s 3 pieces gives 6 pieces, and her 1 piece becomes 2 — the same as Ravi’s 2/6.

q.t: A class of 32 children: 1/2 of them play outside and 1/4 of them read. The rest paint. How many children paint?
q.e: 16 play and 8 read, so 32 − 16 − 8 = 8 are left to paint.
